Title: Kinetic modeling of methanol synthesis from renewable resources

Abstract: In the present paper new detailed kinetic model for the methanol synthesis from  $ H_{2} $,  $ CO_{2} $ and/or CO using a Cu/ZnO/ $ Al_{2}O_{3} $ catalyst is proposed. In contrast to most established models different active surface species for CO and  $ CO_{2} $ hydrogenation are taken into account. It is shown that changes in the relative amounts of these different surface species, which are related to changes in catalyst morphology, play an important role for the dynamic transient behavior. The model is therefore suitable for evaluating new applications in chemical energy storage, where strongly varying ratios of CO and  $ CO_{2} $ are of relevance. The model parameters were fitted to steady state and dynamic experimental data for varying  $ CO/CO_{2} $ feed ratios using global optimization. Identifiability is studied using the Profile-Likelihood method giving rise to a reduced kinetic model.

Model: Simplified kinetic model, steady-state φ
Laws:
(10) [constitutive] Computes the rate constant as a reparameterized Arrhenius function of temperature.
(22) [definition] The equilibrium relations determine the fraction of reduced surface centers.
(23) [constitutive] The relative free-energy contact-surface ratio for Cu and Zn is related to the reaction equilibrium constants and gas partial pressures.
(24) [constitutive] The Gibbs free-energy change and temperature determine the equilibrium constant for reaction 1.
(25) [constitutive] The Gibbs free-energy change and temperature determine the equilibrium constant for reaction 2.
(C-11) [constitutive] The CO hydrogenation rate is calculated from the reversible CO–hydrogen driving term, catalyst state, and surface coverages.
(C-12) [constitutive] The CO₂-to-methanol reaction rate is calculated from its reversible gas-phase driving term and catalyst surface coverages.
(C-13) [constitutive] The reverse water-gas-shift rate is calculated from the CO₂/CO–water/hydrogen driving term and catalyst-state coverage factors.
(C-14) [constitutive] The fractional coverage of ⊙ sites is computed from adsorption of CO, methanol, and CO₂.
(C-15) [constitutive] The fractional coverage of ⊗ sites is computed from hydrogen pressure and its adsorption equilibrium constant.
(C-16) [constitutive] The free reduced-center fraction is computed from water, hydrogen, CO₂, and methanol adsorption terms.
(C-1) [constitutive] A temperature-dependent correlation computes the equilibrium constant for CO hydrogenation.
(C-2) [constitutive] A temperature-dependent correlation computes the equilibrium constant for reaction 2.
(C-3) [constitutive] Temperature correlation for the equilibrium constant of the reverse water-gas-shift reaction.

States (computed by the ODEs):


Inputs (variables no law computes):
- T: Temperature.
- p_{H_2}: Partial pressure of hydrogen.
- p_{CO}: Partial pressure of CO.
- p_{H_2O}: Partial pressure of water used in the model equations.
- p_{CO_2}: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide used in the model equations.
- p_{CH_3OH}: Partial pressure of methanol.

Model-wide assumptions:
- Catalyst deactivation neglected; only reactions (1)-(3) considered.
- Lumped kinetics for reactions (1)-(3).
- Fast steps are at quasi‑equilibrium.
- Two alternatives for φ: quasistatic (Eq.22) or dynamic (Eq.28).

answer.description: This model describes continuous methanol synthesis from CO and/or CO₂ with hydrogen over a Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst, and predicts reaction rates from temperature and gas partial pressures. It combines Langmuir–Hinshelwood surface kinetics for CO and CO₂ hydrogenation and reverse water-gas shift with adsorption coverages, equilibrium relations, and a steady-state catalyst surface-state description. It was fitted to steady-state and dynamic experiments spanning different CO/CO₂ feed ratios.
